mappings.note: What holds animal cells together describes a structural feature of the cell. Not LO-1, because no plant/animal contrast is drawn in the stem.
Viruses as the exception to cell theory is a classification judgement about a group of organisms. Not LO-8, because nothing observed on a slide is being described.
The longest human cell differentiates cell types by structure and size. Not LO-8, because cells are ranked rather than described.
Placing blood among connective tissues classifies tissues by characteristic. Not LO-1, because a class is assigned rather than a contrast drawn.
The cell wall being absent in animal cells is the plant-versus-animal cell differentiation named verbatim in LO-1. Not LO-8, because the answer rests on the comparison.
Matching smooth muscle to organs applies the tissue classification. Not LO-9, because no chart or diagram is produced.
Identifying the components of the nervous system groups structures into an organ system. Not LO-8, because the level is above microscopic description.
Connective tissue identified from support, defence and storage is classification by function. Not LO-1, since one class is named rather than two contrasted.
Epithelial tissue identified from its lining role is the same tissue classification. Differs in content from the connective-tissue item though it shares the outcome.
Nervous tissue identified from stimulus and response is again tissue classification by function. Not LO-5, because the item names the tissue rather than explaining the response.
The functions of the Golgi apparatus describe a cell component. Not LO-5, because no multi-step process is traced.
The vacuole as the storage sac is a microscopic feature to describe. Not LO-1, since no contrast is required.
What the plasma membrane's carbohydrates do describes a component's function. Not LO-5, because no process is explained end to end.
Choosing the correct definition of a cell is the summary description of what the microscope shows. Not LO-9, because no drawing is asked for.
The membrane described by shape, protection and selective permeability is a cell component described by its functions. Not LO-1, because no cell types are compared.
Cytoplasm as the jelly holding the organelles is a microscopic feature. Duplicate in substance of an earlier item and coded the same way.
The nucleus as the largest organelle describes what dominates the field of view. Not LO-1, because organelles rather than cells are ranked.
Chromosomes as threadlike bodies in the nucleus is a description of microscopic structure. Not LO-2, since nothing is classified.
Ordering cells by how many nuclei they contain differentiates cells on a structural property. Not LO-8, because the task is a comparison across cell types.
The nucleus as the control room names a cell part by its role. Duplicate in substance of the control-centre item.
The double-membraned rod that oxidises food is the mitochondrion, identified from its described features. Not LO-5, because the item names the organelle rather than explaining respiration.

ATP as the energy currency belongs to the explanation of how the cell releases and spends energy, not to anything visible on a slide. LO-8 was rejected because ATP is a molecule, not a microscopic feature.
The endoplasmic reticulum identified from transport and synthesis is a cell component described by function. Not LO-5, since no process is traced step by step.
Sac-like structures for synthesis and storage describe cell organelles. Not LO-2, because no classification is required.
Lysosomes as the cell's digestive system is an organelle described by its function. Not LO-5, because digestion inside the cell is not being explained.
Suicidal bags and power houses are nicknames for two organelles to be identified by function. Not LO-1, because no cell types are contrasted.
The structure regulating animal cell division is an organelle identified by role. Not LO-5, because cell division itself is not explained.
Excluding the body that is not part of the solar system is classification of celestial objects, named verbatim in LO-2. This is the only outcome in the frame that covers astronomy content.
Halley's Comet's 76-year return is the defining characteristic of that celestial object. LO-5 was rejected because the item asks for the interval, not for an explanation of why comets return.
Ursa Major placed in the constellation class is classification of celestial objects. Not LO-1, because no two objects are contrasted.
Comparing planets by their number of satellites characterises celestial objects. The frame offers only this astronomy outcome, so it shares the code with its neighbours.

The light year as the unit for astronomical distance is a measurement question, and the only measurement LO in the frame, LO-7, is confined to angles of incidence and reflection. Cited at the competency level deliberately because no learning outcome covers it.
Naming a recognisable star pattern a constellation is classification of celestial objects. Not LO-5, because no phenomenon is explained.
The Sun as the nearest star places a familiar body in the star class. Not LO-1, because no property comparison is drawn between two objects.
Comets defined by their highly elliptical orbits is classification of celestial objects by characteristic. Not LO-5, since the orbit is not being explained.
Asteroids identified by their location between Mars and Jupiter is classification of celestial objects. Differs in content from the comet item though it shares the outcome.
Venus as the morning or evening star identifies a celestial object from how it appears. Not LO-5, because the appearance is not being explained.
Naming the Milky Way places our galaxy in the celestial-object scheme. Not LO-12, because nothing is applied.
Excluding the non-planet is direct classification of celestial objects. Not LO-1, because a class boundary rather than a property is tested.
